subject: Request: Aquila-Blend variant pin & compatibility plan
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aquila Labs <eng@aquila.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Aquila-Blend variant pin & compatibility plan

Folks / Aquila team —

Quick background: Aquila just shipped the blend-v2.1 variant we agreed to intake. Early staging runs show generally good quality but we observed a tokenization/embedding drift for payloads with long trailing whitespace and some sequence-id collisions in our KV cache when using quantized builds. That combination increases tail latency and causes a small but noticeable token mismatch on reranking tests.

Ask: before we open public rollout, product needs a short proposal from infra/runtime for a temporary version pin and a compatibility gating plan (canary %, telemetry signals, rollback criteria). Specifically I want:
- A recommended pin window (e.g. pin blend-v2.1 on hosted for 72 hours or until metric X stabilizes).
- Canary plan (percentage, cohorts, telemetry gating).
- Any runtime/quantization adjustments required (per-request flags, fallback variant).
- Expected cost/throughput delta if we enable the proposed mitigations.

Attached is a compat matrix from our automated intake run (aquila-blend-compat-matrix.xlsx) and a sanitized snippet of the staging canary log that shows the KV cache warnings (staging-canary-runtime-log.txt).

Timeline: product would like a recommendation by EOD Wed so we can align the next week’s ingress schedule.

Samantha — can your eng lead confirm whether blend-v2.1 includes the tokenizer patch you mentioned in the PR notes? If not, is there a backport you can provide?

Thanks —
David

--
David Kim
Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aquila Labs <eng@aquila.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Aquila-Blend variant pin & compatibility plan

Thanks David — quick clarifying q's from product before we lock anything down:

1) Which user cohorts did staging exercise? (SMS / chat / long-form doc snippets) — mixing long-form doc snippets + chat seems to surface the tokenization edge case most often.
2) Do we have a suggested fallback model? If blend-v2.1 is pinned, should we route to blend-v2.0 or a different family for affected requests?
3) Is this safe to treat as a temporary "provisional pin" triggerable by telemetry, or do we need an explicit config change from product/legal to hold ingress?

From a product standpoint we prefer a provisional pin (automated) vs org-level freeze. If infra indicates the KV collisions are symptomatic of a cache key normalization bug, we should probably keep the pin until the backport is validated.

Marcus / Karthik — can you weigh in on what telemetry metric(s) we should use to auto-unpin (e.g. token-mismatch-rate < 0.01% over 100k requests AND median tail latency < 120ms)?

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Model Platform
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aquila Labs <eng@aquila.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Aquila-Blend variant pin & compatibility plan

Laura / team —

Thanks for the detail. Quick engineering readout and a proposed runbook:

- Root cause (prelim): tokenizer whitespace normalization change in blend-v2.1 plus a subtle length-field difference in our serializer for quantized payloads -> leads to KV cache key mismatch. Not a security issue but can impact cache hit-rate and cause rerank divergence.
- Immediate mitigation: provisional pin of blend-v2.1 on hosted routing with a staged canary (start at 1% of traffic for 6 hours, move to 5% for 12 hours, then 20% for 24 hours) OR until telemetry thresholds are met.
- Telemetry gating: token-mismatch-rate (post-prompt normalization) and kv-cache-miss-rate. Proposed thresholds to auto-unpin: both metrics below 0.01% sustained across 100k requests and no increase in 99th-latency above baseline +10ms.
- Fallback variant: route affected requests to blend-v2.0 family (we have v2.0-dev builds already validated for tokenizer parity).
- Runtime flags: add request-level header X-Model-Compat: strict|lenient so we can test lenient mode that performs on-the-fly normalization at cost of ~3% throughput.
- Capacity note: if canary scales to 20% we need to reserve +12% GPU capacity temporarily. Marcus: can you confirm if Dedicated pools can absorb this without impacting commits?

Attachment: small sanitized staging log (referenced in David's attachments) shows the key collisions and a sample payload.

If product signs off I'll add the pin-change PR and the canary automation job to INF-8421. Also recommend we include a DocuSign waiver for the temporary pin if legal wants an audit trail.

-Karthik

From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@aquila.ai>

Date: Wed, 11 Apr 2028 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Aquila-Blend variant pin & compatibility plan

Hi all —

Thanks for the thorough notes and the telemetry thresholds. We reproduced the whitespace normalization regression in our CI after you flagged it and have a small backport patch ready (PR: https://github.com/aquila-labs/aquila-blend/pull/187). The patch restores the legacy tokenizer behavior behind a feature flag and includes a unit test that mirrors your staging case.

We can do the following:
- Push a hotfix branch today and coordinate a staged deploy to your staging fleet by EOD.
- If you prefer the provisional pin, we agree with the canary sequence Karthik suggested. We will also expose a tokenizer-compat header so you can force legacy normalization per request.
- We'll share a short changelog and a signed backport note for audit.

Let us know if you want us to open a temporary support ticket so your infra team can pull the branch directly.

Samantha

--
Samantha Reed
Engineering Manager, Integration
Aquila Labs
